ideas.title: HERMES: Off-Grid Voice and Data Radio Without the Internet
ideas.why_now: HERMES hit Hacker News this week with 169 points and 66 comments, signaling real interest beyond the ham radio bubble.
ideas.angle: Break down what HERMES actually is, who it is for, and whether it overlaps with or competes with tools like Winlink and Meshtastic that everyday hams already use.

ideas.title: zBitx v5.11s: What the New Community Firmware Actually Fixes
ideas.why_now: Version 5.11s dropped this week and is already drawing builder questions, including one op who says his unit died after five days.
ideas.angle: Walk through what is new in 5.11s, who should update and who should wait, and how to approach a community firmware update without bricking your radio. This is a fresh firmware release angle, not a repeat of the earlier quality-control discussion.

sources.label: groups.io BITX20, zBitx died after 5 days

ideas.title: QMX Firmware Roulette: Five Releases in One Week
ideas.why_now: QRP Labs pushed versions 012 through 015 in rapid succession this week, with bug reports and workarounds filling the list.
ideas.angle: Help builders decide when to update and when to sit tight. Cover the practical update process, the biggest bugs that got fixed, and the ones still open. This is a new angle focused on the rapid-fire release cycle, not the earlier general pain-points episode.

ideas.title: Activating a Battleship Radio Room: Museum Ships and Ham Radio
ideas.why_now: A well-liked Mastodon post this week showed a ham briefly activating the historic radio room aboard USS Wisconsin, sparking warm discussion.
ideas.angle: Use the Wisconsin activation as a jumping-off point to explore museum ship stations: how to find them, how to get operating access, and what it is like to make a contact from equipment that once sailed into combat.

ideas.title: Being Kind to Slow CW Ops: The QRS Problem
ideas.why_now: A thread this week about operators refusing to slow down when asked QRS generated pointed replies and personal stories from CW teachers.
ideas.angle: Frame this as practical advice for both sides. New CW ops hear how to handle being steamrolled, and faster ops hear why slowing down costs nothing and gains them a contact. Tie it to real POTA CW moments from the week.

sources.label: Mastodon #amateurradio, new op on CW at POTA

ideas.title: Pi-Star Hotspot From Scratch: One Ham's Weekend Build
ideas.why_now: A Mastodon post this week showed a ham spending a Saturday setting up a Pi Zero W hotspot with an MMDVM hat and connecting a Kenwood TH-D75A, drawing practical follow-up questions.
ideas.angle: Walk through the full Pi-Star build for everyday hams who want digital voice without a nearby repeater. Cover hardware choices, common setup stumbles, and which modes are worth trying first.

ideas.title: ISS SSTV Weekend Is Coming: How to Catch It This Time
ideas.why_now: A new SSTV app for Android and iOS launched this week and hams are already linking it to an upcoming ARISS ISS SSTV event around October 3.
ideas.angle: Give listeners a straightforward prep guide: which frequencies to watch, how to use the new app, and how to decode a clean image even in a noisy urban location. Ties a new tool to an imminent event.

ideas.title: POTA by Bike: Radio in the Parks Without a Car
ideas.why_now: Multiple posts this week showed operators doing POTA activations by bicycle, including an 80 km rainy ride hitting five park boundaries at once.
ideas.angle: Explore the practical side of human-powered POTA: what gear fits in a pannier, how to set up fast, and why going car-free can actually make activations more fun and more manageable for beginners.
